questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to grow apples at home
Why we enjoy crunchy food and what the crunch tells us
Why insects are dangerous to eat
How astronauts cook in space
questions.why: They investigate why we are so attracted to crunchy food.

questions.q: Why does scientist Danielle Reed know so much about apples?
options: She works for an apple company
She has written a book about fruit
She studied apples at university
She grew up in an apple orchard
questions.why: She says she grew up as a small child in an apple orchard.

questions.q: What does the texture of crunchy food tell our bodies, according to Beth?
options: To prepare for tough fibre that builds our teeth and chewing muscles
To eat more slowly
That the food contains lots of sugar and will give us plenty of energy
That we are no longer hungry
questions.why: Beth says it tells our bodies to get ready for the rough fibre needed to develop chewing muscles and teeth.

questions.q: Why is the first bite so important, according to Danielle?
options: It decides how much of the food we will eat during the rest of the meal
It makes the food taste sweeter
It helps us decide if the food is good enough to swallow
It cleans our teeth
questions.why: She says we have to decide whether to swallow, and the first bite 'gives us a ton of information'.

questions.q: Why does Danielle mention finding an eggshell in scrambled eggs?
options: To show that eggs should be crunchy
To give a quick recipe for making scrambled eggs with a crunchy topping
To show that a crunch can also warn us something is wrong
To explain why she doesn't eat eggs
questions.why: She says crunch can show quality 'or not', like an eggshell in eggs – 'That's no good!'

questions.q: What did astronauts on the International Space Station say they missed most?
options: Crunchy food
Fresh water
Hot drinks
Their families' cooking
questions.why: Georgie says crunchy food topped the list of what they missed most.

questions.q: What does celebrity chef Dulsie Mudekwa say about eating insects?
options: She has always loved eating insects ever since she was a small child in Zimbabwe
She only eats them when meat is too expensive
She thinks they taste better raw
She changed her mind and now uses them in snacks, cakes and sausages
questions.why: She says she's now a convert and eats them roasted or makes them into flours, cakes and sausages.

questions.q: How does Beth feel about eating insects?
options: She wants to try them soon
She would rather keep eating apples
She eats them every week
She thinks they're healthier than apples
questions.why: Beth says, 'I think I'll stick to apples thanks.'
